subject: science
domain: Waves and Their Applications in Technologies for Information Transfer
skillName: How We See Objects with Light
intro: We see objects because light bounces off them and travels into our eyes. Light comes from a source, such as the Sun or a lamp, shines on an object, and reflects off the object in all directions. When some of that reflected light enters your eye, you see the object. This is why you cannot see anything in a completely dark room: with no light to reflect off objects and reach your eyes, there is nothing for your eyes to detect. A model with arrows can show light going from the source, to the object, and then to the eye.

items.prompt: Using arrows, model how you are able to see a red apple on a table in a lit room.

steps: Light starts at a source, such as a lamp or the Sun.
The light travels to the apple and reflects (bounces) off it.
Some of that reflected light enters your eye, so you see the apple.
solution.answer: Light goes from the source to the apple, reflects off it, and enters your eye, so you see the apple.

items.prompt: Why can you not see anything in a completely dark room with no light at all?

steps: Seeing requires light to reflect off objects into your eyes.
In total darkness there is no light to reflect off the objects.
With no reflected light reaching your eyes, you cannot see the objects.
solution.answer: Because there is no light to reflect off the objects and reach your eyes.

items.prompt: A student says we see a book because our eyes send out rays to the book. Use the correct model to respond.

steps: Eyes do not send out rays; they receive light.
Light from a source reflects off the book and travels into the eye.
So we see the book because reflected light enters the eye, not because the eye sends out rays.
solution.answer: Eyes receive light; we see the book because light reflects off it and enters the eye, not because eyes send out rays.

items.prompt: What must happen for you to see an object?

steps: Seeing depends on light reaching your eye from the object.
Light must reflect off the object and enter your eye.
solution.answer: Light must reflect off the object and enter your eye.

items.prompt: A flashlight is shined on a mirror in a dark room and you can see the bright spot where it lands on the wall. Explain using the light-to-eye model.

steps: The flashlight is the light source.
The light reflects off the mirror and then off the wall spot.
That reflected light enters your eye, so you see the bright spot.
solution.answer: Light from the flashlight reflects off the mirror and wall, and that reflected light enters your eye so you see the spot.

items.prompt: In a model of seeing a tree outside, name the three parts the arrows should connect.

steps: Seeing involves a light source, the object, and the eye.
The arrows connect the Sun (source) to the tree (object), then the tree to the eye.
solution.answer: The light source (Sun), the object (tree), and the eye.
